problem: Assessing the reliability of a commercial System-1 model on biosecurity-relevant benchmarks, focusing on calibration, selective prediction, and answer-order stability.
method: Audit of a single System-1 model measuring accuracy, calibration (expected calibration error), error detection, selective prediction (accuracy vs coverage), and sensitivity to answer option order; interpretation of vendor uncertainty field as affine rescaling of max probability; analysis of selective prediction curves and permutation averaging.
key_assumptions: The vendor’s uncertainty field is an affine rescaling of the model’s max probability and can be interpreted as calibrated.
main_contribution: A reliability audit revealing moderate calibration (ECE 0.034) and good AUROC (0.820) for a System-1 model on biosecurity benchmarks, identification of substantial answer-order instability (37.4% of items change answer under option permutations), and demonstration that averaging probabilities across rotations improves accuracy, especially when applied selectively to low-confidence items.
datasets: 6,020 multiple-choice items from the Weapons of Mass Destruction Proxy (WMDP), a paraphrase-robust WMDP-Bio variant, and six LAB-Bench subtasks
results: "Once the vendor’s uncertainty field is correctly interpreted, the model is reasonably well calibrated (pooled ECE 0.034) and its top-1 probability separates correct from incorrect predictions (pooled AUROC 0.820). Under four cyclic rotations of answer options, 37.4% of WMDP-Cyber items receive different answers; averaging probabilities across rotations improves WMDP-Cyber accuracy by +3.8 percentage points, and applying averaging only to low-confidence items recovers most of that gain at well under the cost of averaging every item."
limitations: Calibration quality varies across datasets (ECE up to 0.193 on SuppQA due to small item counts)
Answer-order instability indicates sensitivity to trivial perturbations, questioning robustness
Focus on a single commercial System-1 model limits generalizability
future_work: Extend audit to other System-1 models and diverse tasks
Investigate root causes of answer-order instability and develop mitigation strategies
Explore selective prediction approaches that account for permutation instability

relation_to_idea.conceptual_difference: The paper evaluates calibration and selective prediction of a single model for reliability auditing; the idea proposes calibrating multiple diverse models and using common thresholds for routing decisions in collaborative inference.
